newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to privatise infrastructure projects.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to privatise infrastructure projects.

text.p: Thailand plans to privatise new major infrastructure projects in the next few years as its economy further liberalises and expands, Thai Transport and Communications Minister Suwat Liptapallop said on Wednesday.

Suwat told the joint foreign chambers of commerce that projects planned for privatisation by his ministry included inter-provincial bullet trains, highways, a second national airline, a new Bangkok airport and telephones.
The minister said his ministry would soon invite private bids for a license to operate a second Thai national airline.
He said the successful applicant must be prepared to run the new carrier with a minimum initial capital of three billion baht ($120 million).
He said the government planned to seek private participation in building Bangkok's second international airport at its eastern Nong Ngu Hao suburb.
Suwat said private bidders would be invited after designs of the airport and related terminals were completed in September.

The Thai government has invested about 10 billion baht in civic and ground clearance works at the Nong Ngu Hao site. The minister said, however, that the new airport's earlier scheduled completion in the year 2000 could be delayed a few years.
Suwat said up to 12 foreign firms were keen in undertaking future bullet train projects in Thailand.
He said the country's first bullet train was likely to be a 200 km (120 miles) line between Bangkok and the south-eastern industrial province of Rayong.
The minister said the project, estimated to cost about 35 billion baht, was expected to be 40-50 percent financed by the private sector.

Suwat said private investors would also be given a role in government plans to build inter-provincial toll motorways and in Thailand's efforts to double its current six million fixed telephone lines by the year 2001.
